about: KJV word helps: short glosses + example refs. Hub concordance lists a growing subset of lemmas; each entry includes a concordance key for Search. See scripts/README-kjv-word-notes.md.

words.note: Often means self-giving love (caritas), not fundraising or a donation drive.
words.step: In 1 Corinthians 13, read “charity” as steadfast love.
words.why: When kindness feels out of reach, “charity” in the KJV points to steady, self-giving love—not how generous you look.

words.note: Usually manner of life or citizenship, not small talk.
words.step: Ask: “How is my walk?” when you see “conversation.”
words.why: On days you feel scattered, remember “conversation” is often your whole walk with God, not your chat skills.

words.note: Often “living” or “alive,” not fast.
words.step: Pair “quick” with “dead” in context to see alive vs lifeless.
words.why: If “the quick and the dead” confuses you, you are in good company: here “quick” means alive—God’s word speaks to living hearts.

words.note: Treasured possession or special people set apart, not “weird.”
words.step: Hear “treasured” when you read peculiar in Titus 2:14.
words.why: When you feel overlooked, the KJV “peculiar” people are treasures set apart—seen by God.

words.note: Holy Ghost is the Holy Spirit — older English for the same Person.
words.step: Do not read “ghost” as a spooky figure; same Comforter Jesus promised.
words.why: If the old word unsettles you, “Holy Ghost” is the same Comforter—the Spirit Jesus promised.

words.note: Often “go before,” “meet,” or “come first,” not “stop.”
words.step: In 1 Thessalonians 4:15, think “precede,” not “block.”
words.why: When plans feel stuck, “prevent” in older English often meant “go before” or “meet”—God still goes ahead of you.

words.note: Sometimes “allow” or “let,” not only “endure pain.”
words.step: When children are named, “suffer” usually means “let them come.”
words.why: When you read “suffer the little children,” hear gentle permission: let them come—not only pain language.

words.note: Strength, power, or moral excellence going out from Christ — not only modesty.
words.step: In Luke 8:46, virtue is power that went out of Him.
words.why: When you feel drained, “virtue” in the Gospels can mean power that went out from Christ—His strength, not yours alone.

words.note: Often solid food (teaching you chew on), not only animal flesh.
words.step: Contrast milk and meat when growth in doctrine is in view.
words.why: When teaching feels over your head, “meat” is food you chew on—solid truth for a maturing heart, not a slight.

words.note: Grain (wheat, barley), not maize.
words.step: Picture sheaves and harvest, not sweet corn on the cob.
words.why: When harvest language appears, “corn” is grain in the field—bread and provision—not sweet corn by default.

words.note: Fill or populate the earth, not “refill an empty tank” only.
words.step: In Genesis 1:28, God fills the earth with people and life.
words.why: When life feels empty, replenish in Genesis is about filling and fruitfulness under God’s blessing.

words.note: Sometimes “overcome” or “take hold of,” not only “understand.”
words.step: John 1:5: darkness did not overcome the light.
words.why: When darkness feels winning, John reminds you light is not overcome—truth still stands.

words.note: Private inner room for prayer, not a clothes closet only.
words.step: Picture a shut door and secret speech to the Father.
words.why: When prayer feels exposed, Jesus points to a shut door—quiet honesty with the Father.

words.note: Deep affection or compassion — idiom for the seat of feeling.
words.step: Read as “tender compassion,” not anatomy lessons.
words.why: When compassion feels cold, “bowels” is old idiom for deep tenderness—God-shaped affection, not anatomy.

words.note: Often “full of care” or anxious, not merely “attentive.”
words.step: Philippians 4:6 pairs “careful for nothing” with prayer.
words.why: When worry runs the day, Philippians’ “careful for nothing” is an invitation to carry it to God in prayer.

words.note: Often “share” or give materially, not only “talk.”
words.step: Hebrews 13:16 ties sharing with doing good.
words.why: When you want to bless someone, “communicate” in the epistles often means share materially—love with substance.

words.note: Body, human nature, kinship, or weakness — context decides.
words.step: Track whether “flesh” means body, self, or unredeemed appetite.
words.why: When temptation is loud, “flesh” is not only your body—it can mean self-led desire that needs the Spirit’s lead.

words.note: Sheol, grave, or Gehenna by context — not one English place every time.
words.step: Let surrounding verses show whether grave, judgment, or imagery.
words.why: When the word frightens you, let each verse show whether grave, judgment, or imagery—read with context, not panic.

words.note: Will, mind, and inner person — not only emotion.
words.step: “As he thinketh in his heart” is orientation, not only mood.
words.why: When emotions swing, “heart” in scripture is your inner direction—what you treasure and choose—not only feelings.

words.note: Life, self, appetite, or person — overlaps with heart and spirit.
words.step: Ask whether the verse means life, inner life, or appetite.
words.why: When you feel undone, “soul” often means your life before God—breath, appetite, self—He cares for the whole person.

words.note: Breath, attitude, unclean spirit, or Holy Spirit — let the verse choose.
words.step: Capitalization in print helps; in audio, context must.
words.why: When you are spiritually tired, “spirit” might mean breath, attitude, evil spirit, or Holy Spirit—let the verse decide.

words.note: Change of mind that shows in turning — not mere regret.
words.step: Look for fruit that matches the turning.
words.why: When shame is loud, repentance is turning toward mercy—not wallowing.

words.note: Declared righteous before God by faith — not “earned by behavior first.”
words.step: Distinguish standing before God from growth in holiness.
words.why: When your mind replays failure, justification is God’s righteous verdict on everyone who trusts Christ.

words.note: Set apart for God; status and growth both appear.
words.step: Note past tense “were sanctified” and ongoing “be holy.”
words.why: When growth feels slow, sanctification is both God’s gift and daily becoming more His.

words.note: Wrath absorbed; mercy-seat reality — God’s justice and love meet.
words.step: Think “satisfied justice,” not a cold word only.
words.why: When guilt feels unbearable, this word quietly says God’s justice and love met in Christ—for you.

words.note: Counted to your account — Abraham’s faith reckoned as righteousness (idea in Romans 4).
words.step: Follow “reckon” and “impute” in Romans 4 in one sitting.
words.why: When guilt says “not enough,” imputation is God counting faith to you for righteousness—His gift, not your résumé.

words.note: Binding promise God makes and keeps; new covenant in Christ’s blood.
words.step: Old and new contrast in Hebrews is about better promises.
words.why: When promises feel fragile, covenant is God binding Himself—faithful when we are not.

words.note: Tent of meeting; God dwelling with a moving people; shadow of Christ.
words.step: John 1:14: “dwelt” is tabernacled among us.
words.why: When church feels distant, remember God tabernacled among us—He draws near to sinners in Christ.

words.note: Covering of sin; fulfilled in the one final sacrifice.
words.step: Hebrews shows one offering versus repeated shadows.
words.why: When sin feels sticky, atonement is sin covered and answered—pointing to one final sacrifice.

words.note: Bought back — a price paid, ownership changed.
words.step: Tie redemption to ransom language without sensationalism.
words.why: When life feels owned by fear or habit, redemption is being bought back—belonging to the Lord again.

words.note: God’s favor you did not earn — not permission to sin.
words.step: Pair Ephesians 2:8–9 with Romans 6 on new life.
words.why: On days you feel you have to earn rest, grace is God’s favor meeting you before you proved anything.

words.note: Trust resting on God’s word; shows in obedience.
words.step: Faith and works tensions resolve when faith is living.
words.why: When you cannot see the next step, faith is trust anchored in what God has said.

words.note: Deeds — not ground of salvation, yet faith without deeds is dead.
words.step: Ephesians 2:8–10 holds both grace and workmanship together.
words.why: When you fear you are never doing enough, scripture still says true faith shows up in real love and obedience.

words.note: Age, order, or people on earth — context narrows meaning.
words.step: Ask: moral system, planet, or people?
words.why: When headlines overwhelm, “world” can mean creation, age, or value-system—ask which one the verse targets.

words.note: Assembly — local gathered body and Christ’s people overall.
words.step: Building metaphor is people, not brick idolatry.
words.why: When fellowship hurts, “church” is the called-out assembly—people under Christ’s headship, still being sanctified.

words.note: Overseer — pastoral office of care and sound teaching.
words.step: Often overlaps elder; watch context for office vs gift.
words.why: When leadership disappoints, bishop is overseer language—gifted care, answerable to the Chief Shepherd.

words.note: Demons, unclean spirits — Christ’s authority is absolute.
words.step: No fascination — flee to Christ’s word and presence.

words.note: Fermented drink in many uses; wisdom warns excess.
words.step: Let context show celebration, medicine, or warning.

words.note: Judgment image — treading out God’s wrath in Scripture imagery.
words.step: Read as sobering picture, not glee.

words.note: Building, Christ’s body, or believer — track the referent.
words.step: Paul’s “your body is the temple” is personal holiness.

words.note: Often “allow” or “permit,” sometimes “leave off.”
words.step: When Paul says “I beseech you… let,” he means “allow this to be so.”
words.why: When you read “let not,” hear permission to stop—God’s commands often free you from what binds.

words.note: Pattern or example left for others to follow.
words.step: Christ’s steps are the template in 1 Peter 2:21.

words.note: Turn aside from; shun evil.
words.step: Pair with “seek peace” in the same verse.

words.note: Strong desire — not only sexual; can be craving generally.
words.step: Name the desire and bring it to God honestly.
words.why: When desire misleads you, lust is craving that pulls away from God’s good—naming it is the first step toward freedom.

words.note: Be diligent, strive rightly — not only “academic homework.”
words.step: 2 Timothy 2:15 is a workman approved, not proud.
words.why: When the mind races, study is earnest care—to approve what is excellent, not anxious grinding.

words.note: Foreign, alien, or unusual — context decides.
words.step: “Strange trial” is unfamiliar testing, not oddness.
words.why: When you feel like an outsider, strange can mean foreign fire or other gods—keep worship pure and near to God.

words.note: In Acts 17, “very religious” — devout, not “irrational” only.
words.step: Paul bridges from their altar to the unknown God.

words.note: To choose, desire, or please — archaic verb.
words.step: “Listed” can mean “was pleased” or “chose.”

words.note: Expanse or arch — heavens spread out, not modern “firm plate” debates.
words.step: Read poetry as majesty, not modern science footnotes in the margin.

words.note: Boiled or cooked — Jacob’s pottage.
words.step: “Sod pottage” is stew, not turf.

words.note: Knew — past of “wit” (to know).
words.step: Swap in “knew” when it sounds wooden.

words.note: Know — “we wot that” means “we know that.”
words.step: Same root family as “wist.”

words.note: Truly, amen — solemn emphasis.
words.step: When Jesus doubles “Verily, verily,” slow down and listen.

words.note: Perhaps, maybe — not “happily.”
words.step: Think “perhaps,” not emotional happiness.

words.note: At once, soon — immediacy.
words.step: Rhymes with “upon” in rhythm — sense is “right away.”

words.note: Immediately — same idea as “forthwith” in places.
words.step: Narrative speed: obey without dragging feet.

words.note: Immediately or soon — not “eventually” in several texts.
words.step: Check context: sometimes “at once,” sometimes “later” in older English — compare translations carefully.

words.note: Behavior or baggage — context decides (conduct vs what is carried).
words.step: In narrative, “carriage” can mean baggage train; in epistles, sometimes “walk.”

words.note: Skilled, intricate, or prying — context picks.
words.step: Craftsmanship vs forbidden arts — watch the verse.

words.note: Busy oneself in what is not yours — warn trouble.
words.step: Ask: “Is this my lane?”

words.note: Complete, mature, finished — not flawless in every modern sense.
words.step: Hebrews maturity vs milk is a growth picture.
words.why: When you fear you will never measure up, “perfect” often means complete or mature—not impossible personal polish.

words.note: Comforting words or strength — adjective of comfort.
words.step: “Comfort ye” goes with tender speech.
words.why: When you need a steady word, “comfortable” in older English ties to strengthening speech—God speaking courage.

words.note: Put to death — kill sin by the Spirit’s help.
words.step: Not self-harm — Spirit-empowered putting off.
words.why: When sin feels entrenched, mortify means putting deeds to death by the Spirit—kindness, not self-destruction.

words.note: Sincerity, single-mindedness — not “simple-minded.”
words.step: Opposite of double-dealing.
words.why: When you second-guess every motive, simplicity is sincere single-mindedness before God.

words.note: Modesty and reverence — especially in 1 Timothy 2.
words.step: Outward demeanor that matches godliness.
words.why: When culture shouts exposure, shamefacedness is modest reverence—honor, not fear of being seen.

words.note: Condemnation or judgment — legal outcome, not a curse word.
words.step: Serious, not slang — let the text define which judgment.
words.why: When the word sounds harsh, it is serious judgment language in court terms—let scripture define the verdict in view.

words.note: Crowd pressing in — throng around Jesus.
words.step: Physical crowd, not only “pressure” metaphor.
words.why: When crowds surround Jesus in the text, press is a throng drawing near—physical nearness, hunger for Him.

words.note: Increase, grow many — people, blessing, or trouble by context.
words.step: Ask whether growth is godly or grievous.
words.why: When life feels thin or loud, multiply tracks blessing or burden by context—ask which way the verse bends.

words.note: Kidneys — Hebrew idiom for inner affections; KJV uses “reins.”
words.step: Read as “deepest motives,” not biology quiz.
words.why: When desire is hard to name, reins picture inner motives—God tries the heart, not only the face.

words.note: Knowledge — “science falsely so called” is empty knowledge.
words.step: Not modern lab science by default — compare “knowledge.”
words.why: When “science” appears in KJV, it often means knowledge claimed—compare with God’s truth, not modern labs only.

words.note: Empty, worthless, or idols — “in vain” is emptiness.
words.step: “Vanity” in Ecclesiastes is vapor-like emptiness.
words.why: When efforts feel pointless, vain can mean empty or idol—ask what you are trusting besides the Lord.

words.note: Crafty or shrewd — serpent in Eden, not a compliment.
words.step: Moral shade: discern good subtlety vs deception.
words.why: When someone seems too smooth, subtil is crafty—watch serpent language and choose plain truth.

words.note: Power, right to command, or sphere — rulers, parents, Christ.
words.step: All human authority is under God’s.
words.why: When power scares you, authority in Scripture is ordered—Jesus has final say; earthly power is bounded.

words.note: Life, sacrifice, covenant — context shows meaning.
words.step: Trace blood from altar to Christ once for all.
words.why: When conscience accuses, blood in scripture points to life laid down—atonement that speaks better than sacrifice.

words.note: Shameful death and glory — offense and power.
words.step: Boast only in the Lord’s finished work.
words.why: When self is loud, the cross is shame turned to glory—where boasting dies and mercy rises.

words.note: Good news of Christ’s kingdom, death, and resurrection.
words.step: Keep the core facts central when “gospel” is used broadly.
words.why: When truth feels thin, the gospel is the good news of Christ’s finished work—keep the core facts central.

words.note: Set-apartness unto God — moral and positional.
words.step: Pursue peace and holiness together.
words.why: When you feel too ordinary for God, holiness is set-apartness—His gift and daily becoming more like Him.

words.note: Loving-kindness and compassion that is not earned.
words.step: Often used when someone has no right to expect help — yet God gives it anyway.
words.why: In your hardest battles, mercy reminds you God’s kindness is not based on how well you performed today.

words.note: Quiet rest and wholeness that the world cannot give.
words.step: Not the same as calm circumstances — Christ’s gift can hold when life is loud.
words.why: Even when your body hurts or your mind won’t rest, God’s peace can still rule in your heart.

words.note: Power that shows up most clearly when we are weak.
words.step: Paul’s testimony: when I am weak, then am I strong — Christ’s strength, not swagger.
words.why: This is the same strength Paul wrote about — made perfect in weakness.

words.note: Confident expectation anchored in God, not wishfulness.
words.step: Hope is sure because the Promiser is faithful.
words.why: When the future feels blank, biblical hope is steady expectation—because God keeps His word.

words.note: Reverence or terror — context shows holy fear vs panic.
words.step: “Fear not” calms panic; “fear God” awakens reverence.
words.why: When anxiety shouts and worship feels distant, the same Bible pairs “fear not” with holy reverence for God.

words.note: Deep gladness rooted in God — not hype.
words.step: Joy can coexist with grief when hope holds.
words.why: When happiness is gone, joy can still quietly root in Christ—even while you are sad.

words.note: Patience, slow anger — fruit of the Spirit.
words.step: God’s longsuffering is room to repent.
words.why: When patience runs out, longsuffering is Spirit-given room—God patient with us first.

words.note: Strength under God’s hand — not weakness.
words.step: Meekness trusts God with outcomes.
words.why: When you feel pressed to fight every battle, meekness is strength steadied under God’s hand.

words.note: Judgment — guilty verdict; contrast “no condemnation” in Christ.
words.step: Romans 8:1 is the anchor verse for assurance.
words.why: When accusation rings in your head, “no condemnation” in Christ is the door back to peace.

words.note: God’s choosing — comfort and humility, not arrogance.
words.step: Hold election with calling and holiness.
words.why: When you feel unchosen, election is God’s sure purpose—held with humility and holy living, not pride.

words.note: Foreordained purpose — unto conformity to Christ.
words.step: Goal is Christlikeness, not fatalistic gloom.
words.why: When the future scares you, predestination in Romans is unto Christlikeness—His purpose, your comfort.

words.note: Placed as sons — privilege and Spirit witness.
words.step: Cry “Abba, Father” is Spirit-given confidence.
words.why: When “orphan” feels true, adoption is sonship by God’s act—Spirit witness, not paperwork.

words.note: Praying for another — Christ and the Spirit.
words.step: Christ’s priesthood is ongoing help.
words.why: When words fail in prayer, the Spirit and the Son still speak for you—ongoing mercy.

words.note: Trial or enticement — James distinguishes sources.
words.step: God does not tempt to evil; He provides escape.
words.why: When you feel singled out in trial, God does not tempt to evil—He gives escape and faithful company.

words.note: Standing again — Christ first, then His own.
words.step: Hope is embodied — empty tomb matters.
words.why: When death or loss shadows you, resurrection is God’s pledge—Christ’s victory is the church’s hope.

words.note: Age-enduring, eternal — God’s life and punishment both serious.
words.step: Let context show gift of life or severity of judgment.
words.why: When time feels cruel, everlasting life is quality and duration in God—not a rushed slogan.

words.note: Gehenna imagery — Jesus warns seriously.
words.step: Read warnings with trembling mercy — flee to Christ.

words.note: Born again — Spirit’s work, not mere decision talk.
words.step: Nicodemus needed Spirit, not only argument.

words.note: Immersion picture — union with Christ’s death and resurrection.
words.step: Distinguish sign from saving work — faith in Christ saves.
words.why: When identity feels shaky, baptism is union pictured in water—Christ’s, not human prestige.

words.note: Fellowship — often Lord’s supper sense in older usage.
words.step: 1 Corinthians 10 ties cup and bread to one body.
words.why: When you feel alone at the table, communion is fellowship—shared life in Christ with His people.

words.note: Stumbling block — trap or cause to fall.
words.step: Love limits liberty when others stumble.
words.why: When truth offends, “offence” can mean stumbling block—sometimes the issue is hardness, sometimes love warns.

words.note: Merciful giving to the poor — not a performance.
words.step: Pair secret giving (Matthew 6) with a generous heart.
words.why: When you want to help quietly, alms is mercy shown in giving—without needing applause.

words.note: “So be it” — firm agreement and truth.
words.step: When Scripture stacks “amen,” treat it as sealed.
words.why: When words run out, amen is “so be it”—agreement and trust sealed in prayer.

words.note: Sent one — eyewitness ambassadors of Christ with authority.
words.step: Distinguish the Twelve/foundation from every “sent” task today.
words.why: When leadership disappoints, apostle means sent one—authority tied to Christ’s mission, not ego.

words.note: Dress, equip, or set in order — not only “arrange data.”
words.step: In poetry, array is clothing and dignity.

words.note: Fathered, brought forth — genealogy and incarnation language.
words.step: In Matthew 1, trace promise and fulfillment.

words.note: Uniquely brought forth — “only begotten” points to the Son.
words.step: Hold uniqueness without drifting into confusion about the eternal Son.

words.note: Deceived, led astray — Eve and false teachers.
words.step: Name the lie; return to plain Scripture.

words.note: Deceived or fascinated — not stage magic.
words.step: Paul’s point is gospel clarity stolen by confusion.

words.note: Expose, reveal, betray — older verb.
words.step: Context shows whether betrayal or simple disclosure.

words.note: Written certificate — often divorce writing in controversy texts.
words.step: Jesus raises the heart, not paperwork tricks.

words.note: Speech that dishonors God or claims what is His alone.
words.step: Distinguish rash words from the unforgivable hardness Jesus warns of.

words.note: Spot or defect — purity for sacrifice and character.
words.step: Christ is the spotless Lamb.

words.note: Erase debt, remove from record — God’s forgiveness language.
words.step: Contrast with names kept in the book of life.

words.note: Brass or bronze — altar, serpent, sea (symbolic hardware).
words.step: Read as appointed instruments, not lucky charms.

words.note: Often brass/bronze — brazen altar, brazen serpent.
words.step: The lifted serpent points to Christ — faith, not superstition.

words.note: Life-breath from God; also Spirit imagery.
words.step: Every breath is borrowed — live gratefully.
words.why: When you feel fragile, breath ties life to God’s gift—spirit and body held in His hand.

words.note: Husband-to-be — Christ and the church imagery.
words.step: Joy and fidelity — not sentimental fluff.

words.note: Crush or wound — Genesis 3:15 and the suffering Servant.
words.step: Trace hope from the first promise to the cross.

words.note: Small shield — God as protector.
words.step: Pair with “shield” language in the same psalms.

words.note: Load, oracle, or heavy message — context picks.
words.step: “Burden” can mean prophetic word, not only weight.

words.note: Older spelling of burden — same range of meaning.
words.step: Read smoothly as “burden.”

words.note: Measure — hide or reveal light imagery.
words.step: Let good works shine for God’s glory, not vanity.

words.note: Lampstand — tabernacle and “light of the world” imagery.
words.step: Churches as lampstands is responsibility, not décor.

words.note: Dead body — ceremonial laws and sober pictures.
words.step: Use reverence when reading death texts.

words.note: Fleshly, unspiritual — oriented by fallen appetite.
words.step: Not “body is bad,” but “self-run life” vs Spirit-led.

words.note: Providence over chance — used for decisions in narrative.
words.step: God rules what looks random.

words.note: Pure in body and mind — modest love.
words.step: Chastity is wholeness, not shame of being human.

words.note: Discipline for good — Fatherly correction.
words.step: Receive discipline as love, not rejection.
words.why: When discipline stings, chastening is a Father’s training—love that corrects, not abandons.

words.note: Correct sharply when needed — still purposeful.
words.step: Distinguish human abuse from God’s righteous rule.

words.note: Cherubim — heavenly guardians and throne imagery.
words.step: Holy presence is not casual.

words.note: Cling fast or split apart — opposite meanings by context.
words.step: Marriage cleaving vs cursed cleaving — watch the verse.

words.note: Put on — often moral or gospel clothing imagery.
words.step: “Put on Christ” is daily dressing by faith.

words.note: Beautiful, fitting, honorable.
words.step: Modesty can still be comely — dignity without show.

words.note: Entrust, commit, praise — several shades.
words.step: Paul commends people to God’s grace — a tender charge.

words.note: Spoke closely, counseled — intimate talk.
words.step: “Commune with your own heart” is honest self-talk before God.

words.note: Mutilation — Paul’s sharp word for fleshly confidence.
words.step: Contrast true circumcision of heart by the Spirit.

words.note: Confuse, shame, bring to nothing.
words.step: God frustrates proud schemes.

words.note: Inner witness — trained by truth, not mere feelings.
words.step: A seared conscience is dangerous — feed it Scripture.
words.why: When guilt whispers, conscience can be clean or seared—bring it to Christ and His word for a true witness.

words.note: Turn back, restore — soul and direction.
words.step: Conversion is Godward turn, not a mood.
words.why: When you feel stuck, convert is turn—God meets the turned heart with forgiveness and new direction.

words.note: Lie down, rest — sheep and sleep imagery.
words.step: Picture calm when the Lord makes His people lie down.

words.note: Crawling things — creation categories and purity laws.
words.step: Order in creation; humility before the Creator.

words.note: Harsh, fierce — character and consequences.
words.step: Cruel masters contrast the gentle yoke of Christ.

words.note: Nail to a cross — old man, flesh, and Christ’s death.
words.step: Union with Christ’s death is real, not metaphor only.

words.note: Cup of blessing or wrath — what you drink with God.
words.step: Jesus drank the bitter cup for us.

words.note: Calls down curse — solemn, not slang.
words.step: Bless those who curse you — Romans 12.

words.note: Habit, tax, or ordinary practice — context decides.
words.step: “After the custom” is routine — not necessarily holy.

words.note: Removed from covenant people or life — serious.
words.step: Let the weight point you to Christ’s sufficient sacrifice.

words.note: Made unclean — ceremonial or moral.
words.step: Wash in confession and truth — 1 John 1:9.

words.note: Rescue, hand over, or birth — track the sense.
words.step: Deliver us from evil is daily dependence.
words.why: When trouble presses, deliver is rescue language—God as the One who draws you out, again and again.

words.note: Rescue realized — God’s help in trouble.
words.step: Remember past deliverances when new fears rise.

words.note: Disown, refuse — Jesus warns and encourages.
words.step: Self-denial follows Christ — not self-hatred.

words.note: Go away, remove, or die — gentle or solemn.
words.step: “Depart from me” is sober when Jesus says it.

words.note: Treat as nothing — God, wisdom, or neighbor.
words.step: Do not despise small beginnings of grace.

words.note: Consume — Satan as roaring lion; strife devours.
words.step: Stay sober; resist him steadfast in faith.

words.note: Steady effort — faith and virtue.
words.step: Diligence is quiet faithfulness, not panic.
words.why: When you want to quit, diligence is steady care—faithful next steps without theatrics.

words.note: Sensible, prudent — especially Titus 2 maturity.
words.step: Discretion defuses many fires.

words.note: Hypocrisy — hiding what you truly are.
words.step: Love without dissimulation is sincere brotherly love.

words.note: Various — older spelling of diverse.
words.step: Read “divers” as “many kinds,” not scuba.

words.note: Teaching — sound words to build and guard.
words.step: Test all teaching by Christ and the apostles.
words.why: When opinions fly, doctrine is teaching to be held—tested by Scripture, lived with humility.

words.note: Catch of fish; also drain — context picks.
words.step: Miraculous draughts show who rules sea and heart.

words.note: Waste slag from metal — impurity to purge.
words.step: Refining imagery: God purges, not to destroy you.

words.note: Intoxicated — warning and watchfulness.
words.step: Be filled with the Spirit instead — Ephesians 5.

words.note: Mute, speechless — not modern insult.
words.step: Healing stories restore voice — picture gospel opening mouths.

words.note: Dared — older past of dare.
words.step: Swap “dared” mentally when you hit durst.

words.note: Build up — church speech and love.
words.step: Ask: does this word build or tear down?

words.note: Older man; also office of oversight — context.
words.step: Respect and honor where Scripture commands.

words.note: Hold fast — wisdom, seasons, people.
words.step: Ecclesiastes pairs embrace with refraining — seasons.

words.note: Goal, outcome, or final stop — teleology matters.
words.step: “The end of your faith” is salvation of souls.

words.note: Begets, produces — James on lust.
words.step: Trace sin’s birth to death; grace’s birth to life.

words.note: Jealous of another’s good — rots bones.
words.step: Rejoice with those who rejoice — kill envy.

words.note: Letter — apostolic mail to churches.
words.step: These letters are God-breathed rule for faith.

words.note: Wander off course — morally and intellectually.
words.step: Gentle restoration for the erring — James 5.

words.note: Betrothed — purity and expectation.
words.step: Paul’s bridal language is devotion, not drama.

words.note: Value, regard, or reckon — context picks.
words.step: Esteem others better — humility in community.

words.note: Strongly encourage — apostolic voice.
words.step: Exhortation is love with backbone.

words.note: Service only when watched — hollow obedience.
words.step: Serve as unto the Lord — heart, not performance.

words.note: Grow weak, lose heart — God strengthens.
words.step: Do not faint in well doing — season of reaping comes.

words.note: Forbidden spirit contact — witchcraft territory.
words.step: Seek the Lord, not the dead — sober warning.

words.note: Abstain food for prayer — not “quick.”
words.step: Fasting pairs with feasting on God’s word.

words.note: Rich, best portion — offerings and abundance.
words.step: “Fatness” can mean deep satisfaction in God.

words.note: Young fat cattle — feast and sacrifice imagery.
words.step: Parables use feast language — come to the banquet.

words.note: Wonderfully — awe, not terror, in Psalm 139.
words.step: You are fearfully set apart — dignity from the Maker.

words.note: Fierce companions or mockers — rare word.
words.step: Job’s loneliness language — read with compassion.

words.note: Morally foul — rags, speech, lucre.
words.step: Christ clothes the filthy with righteousness.

words.note: Preeminent heir — Israel, Christ, church.
words.step: Christ is firstborn among many brethren.

words.note: First part of harvest — pledge of full crop.
words.step: Resurrection is firstfruits — more glory coming.

words.note: Smooth words that mislead — guard the naive.
words.step: Love speaks truth with kindness.

words.note: According to the flesh — unspiritual mindset.
words.step: Not “body bad,” but “self on the throne.”

words.note: Birds — care of God and parable seed.
words.step: If God feeds fowls, He will sustain you.

words.note: Incense offering — prayer and worship aroma.
words.step: Picture tabernacle worship — Christ is better.

words.note: Voluntary offering — glad heart.
words.step: God loves a cheerful giver — 2 Corinthians 9.

words.note: Speak against, contradict — opposition.
words.step: Christ’s witnesses speak boldly when opposed.

words.note: Beget, produce — archaic verb “gendereth.”
words.step: James: lust conceives and sins when full grown.

words.note: Nations — non-Jewish peoples; grace to the world.
words.step: One new man — Jew and Gentile in Christ.

words.note: Bind up — readiness and service.
words.step: “Gird up the loins of your mind” is alert holiness.

words.note: Belt — priestly dress and John the Baptist.
words.step: Symbol of strength and office — read visually.

words.note: Gather leftovers — mercy for the poor.
words.step: Boaz’s field is a picture of generous provision.

words.note: Bird of prey — eagle-like in prophecy.
words.step: Rare word — read as swift destroying bird in judgment poetry.

words.note: Prostitute — literal and covenant unfaithfulness imagery.
words.step: Spiritual adultery is chasing lovers that cannot save.

words.note: Hurry — sometimes wise, sometimes rash.
words.step: Wait on the Lord beats proud haste.

words.note: Lifted up in pride — God resists.
words.step: Humble yourself under God’s hand — 1 Peter 5:6.

words.note: Listen and obey — covenant call.
words.step: Hearkening is more than ears — it is doing.

words.note: Grief, depression of spirit — God meets it.
words.step: Oil of joy for heaviness — Isaiah 61.
